title: Go: Test Coverage
description: Understand and measure code coverage in Go tests using the built-in coverage tools.

steps.title: Running coverage with go test -cover
steps.description: Write a simple Go package with 3 functions: `Add`, `IsEven`, and `Greet`. Write tests that achieve partial coverage (only test `Add` and `IsEven`). Print the coverage percentage using `fmt.Printf("Coverage: %.1f%%\n", pct)`.
hints: go test -cover outputs coverage to stdout

verification.failureMessage: Print the coverage percentage from go test -cover.

steps.title: Generating coverage reports (coverprofile)
steps.description: Add a test for `Greet` to achieve 100% coverage. Generate a coverage profile using `-coverprofile=coverage.out`. Read and parse the profile to print the total number of blocks and covered blocks. Print using `fmt.Printf("Blocks: %d/%d covered\n", covered, total)`.
hints: The profile format: mode:set then block entries
Each block has start/end line/col and count

verification.failureMessage: Print block coverage statistics from the profile.

steps.title: Visualizing coverage with go tool cover
steps.description: Use `go tool cover -html=coverage.out -o coverage.html` programmatically via os/exec. Parse the HTML to extract covered/uncovered line counts. Print a summary using `fmt.Printf("Lines: %d covered, %d uncovered\n", covered, uncovered)`.
hints: go tool cover -html generates an HTML report
Use os/exec to run external commands
Read the generated file with os.ReadFile

verification.failureMessage: Print covered and uncovered line counts.

steps.title: Focusing coverage with -coverpkg
steps.description: Set up a multi-package project. Use `-coverpkg=./...` to measure coverage across all packages. Write tests that only cover specific packages and show the aggregate coverage. Print per-package coverage using `fmt.Printf("Package %s: %.1f%%\n", pkg, pct)`.
hints: Use comma-separated list or ./... for all
Each package reports its own coverage percentage

verification.failureMessage: Print coverage percentage for each package.
